raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes stale DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse-index rows in reused prefill workspaces
(#63250), while removing the separate full-workspace memset introduced by
#60613.

The combine kernel now initializes its own `-1` sentinels, so the correctness
fix no longer requires an extra CUDA launch or a write over the full aligned
row.

## Claims

- **Bug fix:** every combine output row is fully initialized. Positions in
  `[combined_len, width)` are `-1`, preventing FlashMLA prefill from consuming
  stale indices left by an earlier request or layer.
- **Performance:** for one combine invocation, the 8K ratio-1 path falls from
  `60.93 us` to `26.21 us` (`2.32x`) in eager execution and from `30.62 us` to
  `26.34 us` (`1.16x`) under CUDA graph replay on H100.
- The regression test covers the 12-token #63250 reproducer, bounded replay,
  and rows whose valid prefix fills the entire aligned width.

## Workload mapping

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 40 language-model attention layers and 3 MTP layers.
Its public config contains:

| V4.1 layer type | Count | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `compress_ratio=0` | 5 | sliding-window attention only |
| `compress_ratio=1` | 20 | full compressed cache, up to 512 indexed entries |
| `compress_ratio=2` | 18 | ratio-2 compressed cache, up to 512 indexed entries |

`compress_ratio=4` and `128` belong to the earlier V4 topology and are not
valid V4.1 layer types. They are therefore excluded from the V4.1 benchmark
results below.

Each benchmark number measures one `combine_topk_swa_indices()` call for one
layer in one batch. It is not a complete model step or TTFT measurement.

| benchmark case | serving scenario |
| --- | --- |
| 12-token SWA | Short new chat prompt; exactly the #63250 corruption case |
| 8K SWA | One fresh 8K prompt without prefix cache, at a pure SWA layer |
| 8K C2 | One fresh 8K prompt, at a ratio-2 compressed layer |
| 8K C2, 8 requests | Eight concurrent ~1K prompts, 8K prefill tokens total |
| 8K C1 | One fresh 8K prompt, at a full-compressed-cache layer |
| 16K C1 | One fresh 16K long-context prompt at a full-cache layer |

## Validation

### Correctness

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py -k combine -q
# 11 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  'tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py::test_sparse_flashmla_prefill_smoke' -q
# 2 passed

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_combine_prefill.py
# all hooks passed
```

The regression compares a poisoned `out=` workspace with the explicit CPU row
reference, rather than only comparing one kernel invocation with another. All
12 production warmup variants compile, and aligned/offset tensor views replay
with `jit_monitor(mode="error")`.

### Performance

H100 80GB, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, CUPTI cold-L2 timing, five trials. Values
are the median of per-trial medians; observed trial-to-trial spread is below
4% for the reported cells.

| workload | eager memset + combine | eager kernel sentinels | graph memset + combine | graph kernel sentinels |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 12-token SWA | 39.49 us | 1.60 us | 3.14 us | 1.60 us |
| 8K SWA | 41.66 us | 3.42 us | 6.11 us | 3.42 us |
| 8K C1 | 60.93 us | 26.21 us | 30.62 us | 26.34 us |
| 8K C2 | 60.99 us | 26.18 us | 30.46 us | 26.18 us |
| 8K C2, 8 requests | 50.78 us | 15.65 us | 19.52 us | 15.74 us |
| 16K C1 | 87.84 us | 49.95 us | 64.74 us | 50.08 us |

Using the real 5/20/18 layer distribution, the isolated combine costs for one
fresh 8K prefill are approximately:

| execution mode | before | after | reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| eager | 2.53 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.52 ms |
| CUDA graph replay | 1.19 ms | 1.01 ms | 0.18 ms |

These are per-layer sums from the microbenchmark, not measured model TTFT.

## Details

### Root cause

FlashMLA requires each combined index row to be padded to a multiple of 128.
The combine kernel writes the valid top-k and sliding-window prefix, while
`combined_lens` records its logical length.

The prefill call sites reuse a workspace through `out=`. Before the fix, the
suffix outside `combined_lens` retained indices from an earlier invocation.
FlashMLA prefill processes whole index tiles and can load entries beyond
`combined_lens`; a stale in-range index can therefore address a KV row that
the current call did not write. That stale data can corrupt attention for short
prompts even though the final attention mask is supposed to exclude the entry.

#60613 fixed the stale data by clearing the full workspace with
`combined_indices.fill_(-1)`. This PR keeps that correctness guarantee but
performs the initialization inside the existing combine kernel.

### Implementation

After writing the valid indices, the kernel writes `-1` from `combined_len`
through the aligned row width. A `tl.range` loop skips full rows and processes
only the unused suffix of partially filled rows. The 512-element block size was
selected from a coarse 64/128/256/512 sweep.

Because the kernel now writes every output element, the `out=None` allocation
uses `torch.empty` instead of `torch.full`. Output contents are identical to
the `fill_(-1)` implementation.

### Relationship to #60613

This branch includes #60613's correctness commit and replaces its
`fill_(-1)` implementation with the in-kernel equivalent. If #60613 lands
first, this PR can be rebased and reduced to the performance change.

### Limitations

- The public V4.1 config was used to validate layer types and counts, but the
  checkpoint is not available locally. The H20 end-to-end reproducer and model
  accuracy evaluation were not rerun here.
- The committed benchmark's default case list still contains inherited
  `C4/C128` stress cases. Those should be replaced by the ratio-1 cases above
  before marking the PR ready.
- The reported values are per-layer kernel timings. End-to-end TTFT should be
  collected on V4.1 serving hardware with the target TP/EP and speculative
  decoding configuration.

AI assistance was used to develop this patch, tests, benchmark, and description.
The submitting human must review every changed line and rerun the listed
validation before marking the PR ready.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Keeps sentinel initialization in the existing combine
  kernel and removes a redundant launch and full-buffer pass.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Covers the dirty-workspace contract, short
  prompts, bounded replay, full rows, FlashMLA prefill smoke, and eager/graph
  performance. Checkpoint-level evaluation remains documented as unavailable.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** The core change is small and all pre-commit
  hooks pass.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Separates correctness and performance claims,
  maps workloads to V4.1 layer types, and documents the stacked relationship
  with #60613.
</details>

@@ -0,0 +1,215 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Benchmark DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill index combination.
+
+Compares the current kernel, which writes its own padding sentinels, with the
+previous implementation that cleared the full output workspace first.
+
+Example:
+    .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_combine_prefill.py
+    .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_combine_prefill.py --graph
+
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.cache_utils import (
+    combine_topk_swa_indices,
+)
+
+WINDOW_SIZE = 128
+TOPK_WIDTH = 512
+PREFILL_ALIGNMENT = 128
+
+
+def _make_inputs(
+    seq_lens: list[int],
+    query_lens: list[int],
+    compress_ratio: int,
+    logical_topk: int,
+    seed: int,
+):
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    num_reqs = len(seq_lens)
+    num_tokens = sum(query_lens)
+    query_start_loc = torch.zeros(num_reqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    query_start_loc[1:] = torch.tensor(
+        query_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    ).cumsum(0)
+    seq_lens_t = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    gather_lens = seq_lens_t.clone()
+    ratio = max(compress_ratio, 1)
+    compressed_len = (max(seq_lens) + ratio - 1) // ratio
+    kv_len = 2 * compressed_len + int(gather_lens.max()) + 8
+    topk_indices = torch.randint(
+        0,
+        compressed_len,
+        (num_tokens, TOPK_WIDTH),
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    return (
+        topk_indices,
+        query_start_loc,
+        seq_lens_t,
+        gather_lens,
+        kv_len,
+        compressed_len,
+    )
+
+
+def _run(
+    args: tuple[torch.Tensor | int, ...],
+    out: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
+    *,
+    fill_sentinels: bool,
+) -> None:
+    if fill_sentinels:
+        out[0].fill_(-1)
+    combine_topk_swa_indices(*args, out=out)
+
+
+def benchmark_case(case: dict, args) -> dict:
+    inputs = _make_inputs(
+        case["seq_lens"],
+        case["query_lens"],
+        case["compress_ratio"],
+        case["logical_topk"],
+        args.seed,
+    )
+    topk_indices, query_start_loc, seq_lens, gather_lens, M, N = inputs
+    num_tokens = topk_indices.shape[0]
+    width = (
+        (case["logical_topk"] + WINDOW_SIZE + PREFILL_ALIGNMENT - 1)
+        // PREFILL_ALIGNMENT
+        * PREFILL_ALIGNMENT
+    )
+    indices = torch.empty((num_tokens, width), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    lens = torch.empty(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    out = (indices, lens)
+    combine_args = (
+        topk_indices,
+        query_start_loc,
+        seq_lens,
+        gather_lens,
+        WINDOW_SIZE,
+        case["compress_ratio"],
+        case["logical_topk"],
+        M,
+        N,
+    )
+
+    expected_indices, expected_lens = combine_topk_swa_indices(*combine_args, out=None)
+    _run(combine_args, out, fill_sentinels=False)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(indices, expected_indices)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(lens, expected_lens)
+
+    arms = {
+        "memset_combine": lambda: _run(combine_args, out, fill_sentinels=True),
+        "kernel_sentinels": lambda: _run(combine_args, out, fill_sentinels=False),
+    }
+    samples = {name: [] for name in arms}
+    for trial in range(args.trials):
+        order = list(arms)
+        if trial % 2:
+            order.reverse()
+        for name in order:
+            times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
+                arms[name],
+                repeat_time_ms=args.repeat_time_ms,
+                cold_l2_cache=True,
+                use_cuda_graph=args.graph,
+            )
+            samples[name].append(statistics.median(times) * 1000)
+
+    medians = {name: statistics.median(times) for name, times in samples.items()}
+    return {
+        **case,
+        "num_tokens": num_tokens,
+        "width": width,
+        "device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+        "trials_us": samples,
+        "median_us": medians,
+        "speedup": medians["memset_combine"] / medians["kernel_sentinels"],
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeat-time-ms", type=int, default=200)
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=123)
+    parser.add_argument("--graph", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    cases = [
+        dict(
+            name="short-12-swa",
+            seq_lens=[12],
+            query_lens=[12],
+            compress_ratio=0,
+            logical_topk=0,
+        ),
+        dict(
+            name="8k-swa",
+            seq_lens=[8192],
+            query_lens=[8192],
+            compress_ratio=0,
+            logical_topk=0,
+        ),
+        dict(
+            name="8k-c2",
+            seq_lens=[8192],
+            query_lens=[8192],
+            compress_ratio=2,
+            logical_topk=512,
+        ),
+        dict(
+            name="8k-c4",
+            seq_lens=[8192],
+            query_lens=[8192],
+            compress_ratio=4,
+            logical_topk=512,
+        ),
+        dict(
+            name="8k-c128",
+            seq_lens=[8192],
+            query_lens=[8192],
+            compress_ratio=128,
+            logical_topk=512,
+        ),
+        dict(
+            name="8k-c2-8req",
+            seq_lens=[1024] * 8,
+            query_lens=[1024] * 8,
+            compress_ratio=2,
+            logical_topk=512,
+        ),
+        dict(
+            name="16k-c128",
+            seq_lens=[16384],
+            query_lens=[16384],
+            compress_ratio=128,
+            logical_topk=512,
+        ),
+    ]
+
+    metadata = {
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+        "device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+        "args": vars(args),
+    }
+    print(json.dumps(metadata), flush=True)
+    for case in cases:
+        print(json.dumps(benchmark_case(case, args)), flush=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+    out: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
 ):
     """Run combine_topk_swa_indices and return (indices, lens, expected).
 
@@ -363,6 +364,7 @@ def combine_case(
         topk,
         M,
         N,
+        out=out,
         **image_kwargs,
     )
 
@@ -449,6 +451,50 @@ def test_v41_combine_topk_swa_stops_at_replay_start(cfg, query_len):
     assert indices.cpu().tolist() == rows
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("cfg", "seq_lens", "query_lens", "replay_starts"),
+    [
+        (COMBINE_CASES[0], [12], [12], None),
+        (COMBINE_CASES[1], [40, 12], [24, 12], [16, 0]),
+        (dict(compress_ratio=1, topk=120), [512], [512], None),
+    ],
+)
+def test_v41_combine_topk_swa_initializes_reused_out(
+    cfg, seq_lens, query_lens, replay_starts
+):
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.cache_utils import (
+        combine_topk_swa_indices as combine_v41,
+    )
+
+    kwargs = dict(
+        seq_lens=seq_lens,
+        query_lens=query_lens,
+        spans=[[] for _ in seq_lens],
+        with_image=False,
+        replay_starts=replay_starts,
+        combine_fn=combine_v41,
+        in_range_topk=True,
+    )
+    expected_indices, expected_lens, expected_rows, _ = combine_case(
+        cfg["compress_ratio"], cfg["topk"], **kwargs
+    )
+    stale_indices = torch.full_like(expected_indices, 12345)
+    stale_lens = torch.full_like(expected_lens, 12345)
+    indices, lens, rows, row_lens = combine_case(
+        cfg["compress_ratio"],
+        cfg["topk"],
+        out=(stale_indices, stale_lens),
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(indices, expected_indices)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(lens, expected_lens)
+    assert expected_indices.cpu().tolist() == expected_rows
+    assert indices.cpu().tolist() == rows
+    assert lens.cpu().tolist() == row_lens
+
+
 @pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("cfg", COMBINE_CASES)
 def test_combine_topk_swa_without_image_unchanged(cfg):

@@ -917,9 +917,18 @@ def _compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel(
 # FlashMLA sparse prefill asserts `params.topk % B_TOPK == 0` (see
 # flashmla/csrc/sm100/prefill/sparse/fwd/head{64,128}/phase1.cuh). B_TOPK is
 # 64 for the h_q=64 kernel and 128 for h_q=128; pad to 128 to satisfy both.
